digest.component_or_area: Store event append and ticket directory creation
propositions: Directory creation and first event write were not atomic: os.makedirs occurred outside the write lock while os.replace of the first event happened inside, leaving a window where interruption (kill, timeout, host sleep) could strand an empty ticket directory

Stale interrupted-write debris appears in production as MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH fsck findings: 8 empty ticket directories with the makedirs-then-die signature existed in the production tracker
Solution stages dir+CREATE atomically in a dot-prefixed temporary path and publishes with a single os.rename under the write lock, making the directory and event file visible together
Both single-event stage_and_commit and batch_stage_and_commit paths shared the vulnerable window via _prepare_event and both are converted to use the new StagedEvent staging+promote mechanism
Temporary staging paths use the naming convention .tmp-newticket-<pid>-<uuid4hex> which are already excluded from fsck scanners by existing dot-prefix rules, so no scanner changes are required

A bounded best-effort sweep_stale_staging() at writer start removes only stale .tmp-newticket-* directories owned by provably dead pids, reusing existing lock_owner v2 stamping to defeat pid recycling, without violating the no-writer-cleanup-of-store-data boundary
